jenna_support: FYI we just got flagged by ACME integrator — they see a 403 that looks like an auth failure, but their usage & token look fine. customer says: 'suddenly our production requests started failing with invalid api key' :eyes:
jenna_support: Repro steps from the customer pasted below, trying to sanity-check before escalating to infra:
jenna_support: 1) curl to /v1/generate with their org key 2) random 403 on some requests 3) client shows 'invalid api key' error and stops retrying
jenna_support: They included a trimmed curl + raw response (copied):
jenna_support: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-redwood","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 05 Jul 2026 18:12:31 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 142
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api", error="invalid_token"

{"error":{"message":"invalid api key","type":"invalid_api_key","code":"AUTH_FAILURE"}}
```
jenna_support: Customer notes that the body says 'invalid api key' and their SDK stops and surfaces as auth error, but developer console shows their plan/entitlement is actually over limit for that route (they're hitting a private beta feature).
leo_engineer: A few quick checks: 1) is this the gateway rewriting upstream entitlement errors? 2) is WWW-Authenticate present even for non-auth 403s? 3) did they hit any rate-limiting that we map to 403?
alyssa_sre: I pulled trace for sk-org_XXXX around that time — I see a call chain: edge-gw -> entitlement-service -> route-resolver -> runtime. entitlement-service returned 403 with body {"code":"PLAN_RESTRICTED","reason":"feature_not_enabled"} but edge-gw replaced the response with a minimal auth-shaped payload and added WWW-Authenticate header. looks like a mapping rule in edge that tries to canonicalize 403s to auth-style errors.
alyssa_sre: trace ids: trace-0a1b2c3d, span-edge-9f8e. I attached short log excerpt:
alyssa_sre: ```
[edge] TRACE trace-0a1b2c3d: recv request for /v1/generate org=acme corp. call=entitlement-check
[edge] DEBUG entitlement-service resp: 403 {"code":"PLAN_RESTRICTED","feature":"beta-multiturn"}
[edge] INFO mapping resp -> {"error":{"message":"invalid api key","type":"invalid_api_key","code":"AUTH_FAILURE"}}
```
nora_billing: Confirmed ACME is on a Pro tier that does not include beta-multiturn. They recently requested a trial of beta features but trial wasn't enrolled. Billing side shows an attempted plan change request that failed due to pending invoice. So entitlement-service behavior (403 PLAN_RESTRICTED) is expected.
nora_billing: Problem is the gateway mapping makes it look like an auth failure which blocks our client-side self-serve flow and causes lengthy back-and-forth. Customer thought their API key was revoked.
sam_sales: Customer impact: they churned a dev for ~3 hours trying to find a revoked key. Sales asked for clear messaging to avoid churn during trials. we should make the error actionable: tell them to upgrade/enable trial instead of 'invalid api key'.
leo_engineer: Two immediate action items I see: 1) short fix: stop adding WWW-Authenticate on entitlement 403s and preserve the original entitlement JSON (this will prevent SDK auto-mapping to auth). 2) medium fix: include a specific error_code field we can program client SDKs to surface like "ENTITLEMENT_PLAN_BLOCK" and add docs.
jenna_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can show internal teams. Added a simplified repro that toggles a feature flag to simulate:
jenna_support: ```
# to reproduce locally (dev env)
export RW_API_KEY=sk-test_XXXX
# simulate plan that lacks 'beta-multiturn'
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-redwood","input":"hi","route":"beta-multiturn"}'
# expect: entitlement-service 403 with code PLAN_RESTRICTED, but edge may rewrite
```
alyssa_sre: I've opened infra ticket INF-8764 to change edge mapping rules and preserve non-auth 403 body & headers. Short-term I'll roll a config that strips WWW-Authenticate for entitlement-origin 403s. Rolling to staging in 10m and to prod after validation.
alyssa_sre: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/edge-config/merge_requests/42 (notes in PR).
ops_bot: Deployment scheduled: staging at 2026-07-05T18:40:00Z, prod at 2026-07-05T19:30:00Z (canary first).
jenna_support: I've asked customer to hold while we patch; they said they're fine with a short maintenance window. they also requested a clearer SDK error mapping — do we have an SDK tweak we can ship quickly?
leo_engineer: We can ship SDK change in next patch: treat 403 with body.code in ["PLAN_RESTRICTED","FEATURE_DISABLED","ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED"] as EntitlementError instead of InvalidApiKey, and avoid retrying. I'll draft PR for JS/Python SDKs.
leo_engineer: Example mapping rule (JS):
leo_engineer: ```js
if (status === 403 && body?.code && entitlementCodes.includes(body.code)) {
  throw new EntitlementError(body.message || 'plan or feature gated');
}
```
nora_billing: Also request support-side templated responses for these cases — a short message the Support team can paste: "This request is failing because your current plan doesn't include '<feature>'. To enable it you can start a trial from the console or contact billing (link)."
sam_sales: Putting a note in CRM so AEs don't open a ticket for this in future: CRM note ACME-345: feature trial failed due to unpaid invoice -> causes entitlement 403 masked as auth.
jenna_support: Customer update: they tested a patched SDK (we sent a local build) and now the error surfaces as "EntitlementError: feature_not_enabled - beta-multiturn" so it's clearer. waiting for prod edge change to fully fix retries.
alyssa_sre: Postmortem/next steps:
alyssa_sre: - INF-8764: change edge mapping to preserve entitlement 403 body + remove WWW-Authenticate header for those paths (done in staging).
alyssa_sre: - SDK-112: map entitlement codes to EntitlementError (JS/Py patch).
alyssa_sre: - DOCS-78: add docs page for "403 vs auth vs entitlement" with examples and troubleshooting checklist.
jenna_support: I'll follow up with the customer after prod rollout and share the docs. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
